config.title: Change Detection & Performance

intro.title: Change Detection & Performance
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a user interface that demonstrates Angular's change detection system and learn how to optimize its performance. You'll create components with different change detection strategies and implement techniques like OnPush strategy, trackBy functions, and async pipes to improve application performance. The core concept focuses on understanding how Angular monitors data changes in your application and updates the DOM efficiently. You'll work with Angular's ChangeDetectionStrategy, ChangeDetectorRef service, and performance monitoring tools to identify and resolve performance bottlenecks. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand when and how Angular triggers change detection cycles and how to write more performant Angular applications.
intro.usecase: Change detection optimization is crucial for high-performance Angular applications like real-time dashboards, trading platforms, and social media feeds where data updates frequently. Large enterprise applications with complex component trees, such as project management tools or CRM systems, rely on efficient change detection to prevent UI lag when displaying thousands of records or updating multiple charts simultaneously. E-commerce platforms use OnPush change detection strategy for product catalogs and shopping carts to ensure smooth user interactions even with extensive product listings. Financial applications and analytics dashboards implement custom change detection strategies to handle streaming data updates without compromising user experience during critical operations.

objectives: Implement OnPush change detection strategy to optimize component performance
Configure async pipe to handle observable data streams efficiently
Apply trackBy functions to control ngFor rendering behavior
Construct immutable data updates to trigger change detection properly
Manipulate ChangeDetectorRef to manually control detection cycles
Integrate performance monitoring tools to measure change detection impact
Update component architecture to minimize unnecessary re-renders

steps.title: Import Angular Component and ChangeDetectionStrategy
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Component decorator and ChangeDetectionStrategy enum from the Angular core package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple items from a library
import { Router, ActivatedRoute } from '@angular/router';

successCriteria: Component and ChangeDetectionStrategy are imported from '@angular/core'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing both Component and ChangeDetectionStrategy from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both Component and ChangeDetectionStrategy from '@angular/core' using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent
steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator, setting the selector to 'app-root' and template to display 'Change Detection Demo'
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator above a class declaration. The decorator should include selector and template properties.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, ChangeDetectionStrategy } from '@angular/core';

// Add the AppComponent with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: A properly decorated Angular component class that can serve as the root component
successCriteria: AppComponent class is created with @Component decorator containing selector 'app-root' and a template
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your component has both the @Component decorator and the class declaration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent needs the @Component decorator with selector and template properties, followed by the class declaration.

steps.title: Initialize counter state and expensive data
steps.instruction: Add a counter property initialized to 0 and an expensiveData property as an array with sample items inside the AppComponent class
steps.hint: Define counter as a number property and expensiveData as an array property directly in the component class body
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have counter and expensiveData properties to demonstrate change detection behavior
successCriteria: counter property is initialized to 0 and expensiveData property is initialized as an array with sample data
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure both counter (number) and expensiveData (array) properties are defined with initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add counter as a number property set to 0 and expensiveData as an array property with some sample items inside the component class.

steps.title: Create expensive computation method
steps.instruction: Create a method named 'expensiveComputation' inside the AppComponent class that simulates heavy processing by running a loop from 0 to 1000000 and returning the final count
steps.hint: Add a method that uses a for loop to simulate expensive processing. The method should iterate many times to demonstrate performance impact.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have an expensiveComputation method that performs a heavy computation loop
successCriteria: Method named 'expensiveComputation' is defined that runs a loop and returns a value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your method is named 'expensiveComputation' and includes a loop that processes many iterations.
steps.feedbackWrong: Not quite right. Create a method called 'expensiveComputation' inside the AppComponent class that uses a for loop to simulate heavy processing.

steps.title: Define increment counter method
steps.instruction: Add an increment method that increases the counter by 1
steps.hint: Create a method inside the AppComponent class that updates the counter property by adding 1 to its current value
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have an increment method that increases the counter property
successCriteria: An increment method is defined that updates the counter property by adding 1
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your method increases the counter by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a method that updates the counter property by incrementing its value.

steps.title: Create the component template with counter display
steps.instruction: Update the template to display the current counter value and add an increment button
steps.hint: Replace the existing h1 element with a div containing both the counter display and a button. Use interpolation to show the counter value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: template with interpolation and button template: `

Count: {{count}}

`
steps.expectedOutcome: The template displays the counter value using interpolation and includes a button for incrementing
successCriteria: Template contains interpolation to display counter value and includes an increment button
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're displaying the counter value with interpolation and have included a button.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template needs to show the counter value using {{counter}} and include a button element. Check your template syntax.

steps.title: Add expensive computation to template
steps.instruction: Inside the template, after the h1 heading, add a paragraph that displays the result of calling the expensiveComputation method directly in the template
steps.hint: Call the method using expensiveComputation() within Angular's interpolation syntax to show how method calls in templates can impact performance
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: calling a method in template

Result: {{calculateValue()}}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element is added to the template that calls the expensiveComputation method, demonstrating performance impact of method calls in templates
successCriteria: Template contains a paragraph that calls expensiveComputation() method using Angular interpolation
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're calling the expensiveComputation() method with parentheses inside the template using Angular's interpolation syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Not quite right. You need to add a paragraph that calls the expensiveComputation() method directly in the template. This will help demonstrate the performance impact of method calls in templates.

steps.title: Add performance monitoring logs
steps.instruction: Add console.log statements to both the expensiveComputation method and the increment method to track when these operations execute during change detection cycles.
steps.hint: Place console.log at the beginning of each method to see when they run. This helps understand Angular's change detection timing.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both methods will log to the console when executed, allowing you to observe when Angular triggers change detection and runs expensive operations.
successCriteria: Console.log statements are added to both expensiveComputation and increment methods to track their execution.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to add console.log statements to both the expensiveComputation and increment methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add console.log statements at the beginning of both methods to track when they execute during change detection.

steps.title: Optimize with OnPush change detection strategy
steps.instruction: Add ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to the component decorator's changeDetection property to optimize performance by reducing unnecessary change detection cycles.
steps.hint: In the @Component decorator, add a changeDetection property and set it to ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush. This tells Angular to only check for changes when input properties change or events are triggered.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component decorator now includes the OnPush change detection strategy, which will reduce the frequency of change detection cycles and improve performance by only checking for changes when necessary.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a changeDetection property set to ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track! Make sure you're adding the changeDetection property to the @Component decorator and setting it to ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush.
steps.feedbackWrong: add the changeDetection property inside the @Component decorator and set its value to ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush. This will optimize the component's change detection behavior.

steps.title: Create child component with OnPush strategy
steps.instruction: Create a new child component named ChildComponent that uses OnPush change detection strategy and accepts an input property
steps.hint: Define a component decorator with OnPush strategy and use @Input() decorator for the input property
steps.expectedOutcome: A child component is created with OnPush change detection strategy and an input property to receive data from the parent component
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined with @Component decorator, uses ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, and has an @Input() property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your component uses ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush and includes an @Input() property to receive data from the parent.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a component with the @Component decorator that includes changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush and an @Input() property.

steps.title: Add child component to parent template
steps.instruction: Add the ChildComponent to the parent template below the expensive computation display and pass the counter value through an input property
steps.hint: Include the child component selector in the template and bind the counter property using square brackets for property binding
steps.analogousExample:
// Including child component with input binding
<app-user-profile [userId]="currentUserId"></app-user-profile>
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent is included in the parent template with the counter value passed as an input property
successCriteria: The template includes <app-child> with [count]="counter" property binding
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to include both the child component selector and bind the counter value using property binding syntax [count]="counter".
steps.feedbackWrong: The child component needs to be added to the template with property binding. Use <app-child [count]="counter"></app-child> to pass the counter value to the child.

steps.title: Test and compare performance improvements
steps.instruction: Run the application in your browser and open the developer console to observe how the OnPush change detection strategy reduces the number of expensive computations compared to the default strategy
steps.hint: Look for the console logs that show when expensive computations run - with OnPush, you should see fewer logs when clicking the increment button
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: testing performance in browser
console.log('Performance test complete');
steps.expectedOutcome: The application runs in the browser with console logs showing performance improvements from OnPush change detection strategy
successCriteria: Console logs demonstrate reduced expensive computation calls when using OnPush change detection strategy
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to observe the console logs to see the performance difference between default and OnPush change detection.
steps.feedbackWrong: Run the application in your browser and open the developer console to observe the performance improvements from OnPush change detection.
